mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen three consecutive weeks (-29.7 to -30.1 to -31.0 to -22.7), with the sharpest gain in the latest week, signaling resumption of commuting routines. This drives ancillary retail trips (lunch, shopping on the way home), lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -31.0 to -22.7 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is not higher than the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing to rise, falsifying the commuting-driven retail lift mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has recovered steadily from -67.0 to -57.0 over four weeks. If TRANSIT crosses above -55 (a meaningful threshold indicating near-normal public transport use), it signals broader mobility normalization that will push RETAIL_REC upward within two weeks as transit-dependent shoppers return to retail precincts.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -55 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -67.0 to -57.0 over the snapshot period
failure_condition: TRANSIT crosses above -55 but RETAIL_REC fails to rise within the subsequent two weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines instead, rejecting the threshold linkage.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise together in the same week (as seen in the latest observation, WORKPLACES +8.3pts and TRANSIT +1.6pts week-on-week), the combined effect of commuting and transit use creates a compounding boost to retail foot traffic that exceeds the sum of either series acting alone, raising RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved simultaneously in the t-0w week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 4 weeks is no greater than what would be predicted by WORKPLACES or TRANSIT alone, indicating no compounding interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined steadily from 13.4 to 8.3 over four weeks, indicating people are spending less time at home. In a reopening regime this behavioral shift away from home-bound activity predicts increased out-of-home retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks; the same RESIDENTIAL decline would not predict retail gains in a steady-state or lockdown regime where substitution to other categories (e.g., parks) dominates.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 13.4 to 8.3 over the four-week snapshot
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL continues to decline but RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next four weeks, or the relationship only holds when regime is reopening and fails when regime shifts to steady state.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility dropped sharply from -16.1 to -37.0 in the latest week, likely reflecting a seasonal weather event (e.g., rain) that temporarily suppressed outdoor activity. This short-term seasonal shock is expected to partially reverse within one week, with displaced outdoor recreation substituting toward indoor retail, producing a modest short-term uptick in RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -16.1 to -37.0 in the final observed week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following the sharp PARKS decline, or PARKS itself does not rebound, indicating the drop was not a transient seasonal/weather shock.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has plateaued over the last two weeks (-13.1 then -14.0, a change under 2 points), suggesting the initial post-lockdown recovery surge has exhausted its momentum. This saturation signal predicts flat-to-negative RETAIL_REC movement over the next four weeks as pent-up demand is already satisfied.
candidate_trigger: week-on-week change in RETAIL_REC stays below 2 points in absolute value for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC changed only from -13.1 to -14.0 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC resumes a clear upward trend (greater than 3 points week-on-week growth) despite the plateau, rejecting the saturation hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has remained low and stable (1.7, 4.7, 4.4, 1.6), showing no panic-buying spikes that typically precede announcements of tightened restrictions. This stability signals an absence of imminent policy tightening, supporting continued gradual recovery in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed within a narrow 1.6-4.7 range across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining stable, indicating the absence-of-panic-buying signal does not predict retail direction.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of rising TRANSIT (less negative) and falling RESIDENTIAL together indicates a behavioral shift from home-based to out-of-home, transit-enabled activity. When both series move in these directions simultaneously, the joint effect amplifies RETAIL_REC growth beyond what either series predicts alone within the coming week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises and RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:in t-0w TRANSIT improved to -57.0 while RESIDENTIAL fell to 8.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following simultaneous TRANSIT improvement and RESIDENTIAL decline, or the joint effect is no larger than either series' individual predicted effect.
